mainTopic: Going beyond the letter of the law, and the search for רבי מאיר's source for liability for indirect damage (דינא דגרמי)
overview: The amud opens with the end of a דרשה on שמות 18:20, which reads each word of the פסוק as a separate duty and ends with acting לפנים משורת הדין. Then ריש לקיש shows a coin to רבי אלעזר, who says it is good, and ריש לקיש says, 'See, I am relying on you.' רבי אלעזר asks whether that means he must pay if he is wrong, since ריש לקיש himself said that paying for indirect damage (דינא דגרמי) is only רבי מאיר's view. ריש לקיש answers that we do hold like רבי מאיר. The גמרא then asks which ruling of רבי מאיר teaches דינא דגרמי. It tries a judge who ruled wrongly, a dyer who used the wrong color, and a man who spread his vine over a friend's grain. Each one is pushed away because the person did the damage directly, with his own hands. Finally the גמרא begins a fourth source, a ברייתא about a vineyard fence that broke open, and that case continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The end of the דרשה: the duty to go beyond the letter of the law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a word-by-word דרשה on the פסוק 'והודעת להם את הדרך ילכו בה ואת המעשה אשר יעשון', ending with לפנים משורת הדין.
steps.simpleTranslation: '[Make known to them]' means the core of their life (Torah study). 'The way' means acts of kindness. 'They must walk' means visiting the sick. 'In it' means burial. 'The work' means the law. 'That they must do' means going beyond the letter of the law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining each word of the פסוק as a different duty. The last duty is acting לפנים משורת הדין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word of the פסוק is read as a separate obligation. The pair 'את המעשה' and 'אשר יעשון' shows a difference: the first is the strict law (דין), and the second is doing more than the law strictly demands. So going beyond the letter of the law is presented as something the Torah itself asks of us.

keyTerms.meaning: going beyond the letter of the law

steps.whatToRemember: The last words of the פסוק teach that a person should act לפנים משורת הדין, beyond what the strict דין requires.
steps.whyThisMatters: This דרשה closes the discussion from the previous page about a coin expert acting לפנים משורת הדין. The next story asks a different question: whether a coin expert who errs must pay even by the strict דין (דינא דגרמי).

phrases.english: the core of their life.
phrases.notes: This finishes a line from the previous page explaining 'והודעת להם' (שמות 18:20) as Torah study.

phrases.english: "The way": this is acts of kindness.
"They must walk": this is visiting the sick.
"In it": this is burial.
"The work": this is the law.
"That they must do": this is beyond the letter of the law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a דרשה begun on the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Torah requires kindness, visiting the sick, burial, keeping the law, and going beyond the letter of the law.

steps.title: ריש לקיש shows a coin to רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש has רבי אלעזר check a coin. רבי אלעזר says it is good, and ריש לקיש tells him, 'See, I am relying on you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש showed a dinar to רבי אלעזר. He said: It is good. He said to him: See that I am relying on you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story about checking a coin. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's words 'I am relying on you' seem to hint that רבי אלעזר is now responsible if he is wrong. That hint is what רבי אלעזר will question in the next step.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish showed him
a dinar, to Rabbi Elazar.
phrases.notes: He wanted רבי אלעזר to check whether the coin was real and good.

phrases.english: He said: It is good.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲזִי דַּעֲלָךְ קָא סָמַכְינָא.
phrases.english: He said to him: See that I am relying on you.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אַחְוִי לֵיהּ דִּינָרָא לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story about responsibility for advice on a coin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The case is a coin checked and approved by an expert, with the owner saying he relies on him.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר asks: must I really pay if I am wrong?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks what 'relying on me' would mean. Would he have to replace the coin if it were bad? ריש לקיש himself said that paying for indirect damage (דינא דגרמי) is the view of רבי מאיר, which seems to mean we do not follow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: When you rely on me, what does that mean? That if it turns out bad, I must exchange it for you? But you are the one who said: It is רבי מאיר who judges דינא דגרמי. Doesn't that mean it is רבי מאיר, and we do not hold like him?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר challenges ריש לקיש's hint that he is responsible for the coin. He uses ריש לקיש's own earlier statement against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Approving a bad coin causes loss only indirectly (גרמי). ריש לקיש had said that liability for גרמי is only רבי מאיר's view. When a view is pinned on one named תנא, that often suggests the הלכה is not like him. So רבי אלעזר thinks he would not have to pay.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר is not saying he was wrong about the coin. He is asking whether he would be legally liable if he were wrong.

phrases.english: He said to him: When you rely on me,
what is that coming to say?
That if it is found to be bad,
I must exchange it for you?
But you are the one who said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר הוּא, דְּדָאֵין דִּינָא דִּגְרָמֵי.
phrases.english: It is Rabbi Meir who rules liability for indirect damage.
What, does it not mean: it is Rabbi Meir,
and we do not hold like him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the hint behind 'I am relying on you' in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the coin checker must pay if his approval was wrong.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ריש לקיש himself said that liability for גרמי is רבי מאיר's view, which implies the הלכה is not like him, so no payment is due.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: we do follow רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that he meant the rule is רבי מאיר's, and we do hold like him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No. It is רבי מאיר, and we hold like him.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers by explaining what his earlier statement meant. Naming רבי מאיר was not a rejection of the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר read 'it is רבי מאיר' as meaning 'only רבי מאיר, and not the הלכה.' ריש לקיש says he meant it as the source of a ruling we accept. So דינא דגרמי is binding, and a coin checker who errs may have to pay.
steps.whatToRemember: According to ריש לקיש, the הלכה follows רבי מאיר and one is liable for דינא דגרמי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This makes liability for indirect damage, like bad professional advice, a practical issue. The גמרא will now look for the source in רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: He said to him: No,
it is Rabbi Meir, and we do hold like him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא, רַבִּי מֵאִיר – וּסְבִירָא לַן כְּווֹתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אלעזר's challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying what the earlier statement meant
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Naming רבי מאיר meant the הלכה is not like him.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is רבי מאיר's view, and the הלכה follows him.

steps.title: Which ruling of רבי מאיר is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which ruling of רבי מאיר teaches דינא דגרמי, starts to suggest one, and gives a memory aid for four of his rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which ruling of רבי מאיר? If we say it is this ruling of רבי מאיר... (Memory aid: ד, ל, מ, פ.)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי מאיר teaches liability for indirect damage. This is a setup line: it is about to test several of his rulings one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אילימא' signals a first suggestion that will probably be pushed back. The memory aid letters ד׳ ל׳ מ׳ פ׳ list the four rulings of רבי מאיר that are coming next.

phrases.english: Which ruling of Rabbi Meir?
If we say it is this ruling of Rabbi Meir
(Dalet, Lamed, Mem, Peh: a memory aid)
phrases.notes: These letters stand for the four rulings coming next: דן (judged), לצבוע (to dye), מסכך (covers), פרצה (broke open).

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר? אִילֵימָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the source of the רבי מאיר ruling mentioned in steps 3 and 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which teaching of רבי מאיר shows that one is liable for דינא דגרמי?

steps.title: First suggestion: the judge who ruled wrongly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the source is the משנה about a judge who made a mistake and must pay from his own pocket.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: a judge decided a case. He acquitted the one who was really liable, or made liable the one who was really innocent. Or he called something pure impure, or something impure pure. What he did stays done, and he must pay from his own house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first answer to the question from step 5. It quotes a משנה where a judge who ruled wrongly has to pay for the loss himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The judge did not touch anyone's money. He only gave a ruling, and the loss came about because of that ruling. So it looks like indirect damage, and if he still pays, this would be a source for דינא דגרמי.

keyTerms.meaning: Judged a case; gave a legal ruling
Acquitted, ruled the person does not owe
Ruled the person is liable, must pay
What he did is done; the ruling stays in place
He pays from his own house, from his own money

phrases.english: As we learned: if a judge judged a case,
and acquitted the one who was liable,
or made liable the one who was innocent,

phrases.aramaic: טִימֵּא אֶת הַטָּהוֹר; טִיהֵר אֶת הַטָּמֵא –
phrases.english: or declared the pure impure, or declared the impure pure –
what he did is done,
and he must pay from his own house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first answer to step 5's question of where רבי מאיר teaches דינא דגרמי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which ruling of רבי מאיר shows liability for indirect damage?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה of a judge who ruled wrongly and pays from his own money.

steps.title: Rejected: the judge handled the money himself
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that the judge's משנה is talking about a judge who physically took the money and handed it over, so it is direct damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it said about that משנה: רבי אילעא said in the name of רב, this is only when the judge took the money and gave it over with his own hand!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the first suggestion. According to רב, the judge in that משנה pays only because he handed over the money himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the judge actually took money from one person and gave it to the other, he caused the damage with his own hands. That is direct damage, not גרמי. So this משנה tells us nothing about indirect damage.

keyTerms.meaning: It was said about it; a later teaching that explains an earlier source
Took and gave by hand; physically moved the money himself

phrases.english: But wasn't it said about it,
Rabbi Ile'a said that Rav said:
and this is where he took and gave with his hand!
phrases.notes: He means the judge himself took the money from one side and handed it to the other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 6's source by narrowing the case to direct action.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the judge's משנה as a source for דינא דגרמי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The judge physically moved the money, so the damage is direct, not indirect.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the judge is free from paying. It only says his paying comes from direct action, so the case cannot teach us about indirect damage.

steps.title: Second suggestion: the dyer who used the wrong color
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a new source: a dyer who dyed the wool the wrong color, where רבי מאיר says he pays the value of the wool.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is the ruling of רבי מאיר, as we learned: someone gave wool to be dyed red, and the dyer dyed it black, or black and he dyed it red. רבי מאיר says: the dyer gives him the value of his wool.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the judge's case did not work, the גמרא tries a second ruling of רבי מאיר, about a dyer who used the wrong color.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dyer did not destroy the wool. He only colored it differently than he was asked, yet רבי מאיר makes him pay for the wool. The גמרא suggests that this is liability for a loss that only came about in a roundabout way.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; drops the last idea and offers a new one

phrases.english: Rather, it is this ruling of Rabbi Meir –
as we learned: if wool was given to dye red for him
phrases.notes: The words 'gave wool to a dyer' are not written. The גמרא assumes you know the case.

phrases.english: and he dyed it black,
or black, and he dyed it red –

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: נוֹתֵן לוֹ דְּמֵי צַמְרוֹ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: he gives him the value of his wool.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר – דִּתְנַן: לִצְבּוֹעַ לוֹ אָדוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 7 rejected the judge's case, the גמרא offers a second source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which ruling of רבי מאיר shows liability for indirect damage?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dyer who dyed the wool the wrong color and pays its value.

steps.title: Rejected: the dyer acted with his own hands
steps.stepSummary: The dyer put the wrong dye on the wool himself, so this is direct damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, he does the damage directly with his hands!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the dyer source in a few words. The dyer himself put the dye on the wool.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dyer physically changed the wool, so the damage is direct. Making him pay proves nothing about damage that is only caused indirectly.

phrases.english: There he does it with his hands!

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the dyer's case as a source for דינא דגרמי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The dyer changed the wool directly with his own hands.

steps.title: Third suggestion: the vine spread over a friend's grain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a third source: someone who spreads his vine over his friend's grain makes it forbidden as כלאים and must pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is the ruling of רבי מאיר, as we learned: one who spreads his grapevine over his friend's grain has made it forbidden, and he must pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a third ruling of רבי מאיר. Someone spreads his vine over a friend's grain, which makes the grain forbidden, and he has to pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The grain was not physically harmed. It became forbidden only because of the איסור of כלאי הכרם. That looks like indirect damage, so it seems to be a good source for דינא דגרמי.

keyTerms.meaning: The איסור against growing grain together with a vineyard

phrases.english: Rather, it is this ruling of Rabbi Meir –
as we learned: one who spreads his grapevine
over his friend's grain –
has made it forbidden, and he is liable.
phrases.notes: 'קידש' here means the grain and vine became forbidden because they grew together as כלאים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר – דִּתְנַן: הַמְסַכֵּךְ גַּפְנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 9 rejected the dyer, the גמרא offers a third source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which ruling of רבי מאיר shows liability for indirect damage?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The person who spreads his vine over his friend's grain and must pay.

steps.title: Rejected: spreading the vine is also direct action
steps.stepSummary: The person spread the vine with his own hands, so this case is also direct damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, he does it directly with his hands!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the vine source with the same answer it gave for the dyer. The person spread the vine himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spreading the vine over the grain is his own physical act, and that act is what makes the grain forbidden. So this is also direct damage, and the search for a real source of דינא דגרמי goes on.

keyTerms.meaning: Damage done directly, by one's own act

steps.whatToRemember: All three suggested sources (the judge, the dyer, the vine) are pushed away for the same reason: the person did the damage directly, with his own hands. A true source for דינא דגרמי must be a case where the person did not do the damage himself.

phrases.english: There too he does it with his hands!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 10's source with the same reasoning as step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the vine case as a source for דינא דגרמי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Spreading the vine is a direct physical act.

steps.title: A fourth suggested source: the broken vineyard fence
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes a new source for רבי מאיר's view: a ברייתא about a vineyard partition that broke open.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the source must be this ruling of רבי מאיר, as a ברייתא teaches: a vineyard's partition that broke open...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the vine-spreading case and starts a new suggested source from רבי מאיר. This line only sets up the case; the ruling itself comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier cases were rejected because the person did the damage with his own hands. Here a fence simply broke on its own, so the owner did nothing directly. If רבי מאיר still makes him responsible, that would show he holds a person pays for indirect damage (דינא דגרמי).

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Drops the earlier suggestion and offers a new one

phrases.english: Rather, it is this ruling of רבי מאיר, as it was taught:
A vineyard's partition that broke open,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the vine-spreading case was pushed off as direct damage (step 11), the גמרא offers a fresh source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where do we see that רבי מאיר holds a person pays for indirect damage?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא of רבי מאיר about a vineyard partition that broke open (the ruling continues next).
